growth_story.headline: Senegal's income per person barely moved for decades, then climbed from the late 1990s; new oil and gas lifted growth just as a hidden-debt crisis broke.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in Senegal was lower in 1990 than in 1960, and from 1990 to 1997 it shrank by 0.8 percent a year. After the CFA franc devaluation of January 1994 and years of stabilization and reform, growth turned up in 1998, and from 1998 to 2025 income per person grew 1.8 percent a year; it only passed its 1960 level in 2010. That long era ran at two speeds: 0.9 percent a year over 2006–2015, years the IMF called sluggish, then 2.7 percent over 2016–2025 as the Plan Sénégal Emergent got under way. Oil from the Sangomar field began flowing in 2024, 2025 was the first full year of oil and gas output, and income per person rose 4.0 percent in 2024 and 4.3 percent in 2025, reaching its highest level on record. At the same time, government-led investigations found that spending and debt in 2019–2023 had been far larger than reported, and the World Bank expects growth to slow as oil output eases from its 2025 peak.

threads.title: Devaluation and the late-1990s turn
threads.text: The CFA franc, which Senegal shares with its neighbours, was devalued in January 1994. The IMF and World Bank later described a record of stabilization and reform after it, with output growing strongly in the late 1990s, and the data show growth turning up in 1998.

threads.title: A sluggish decade to 2015
threads.text: Income per person grew only 0.9 percent a year over 2006–2015. By 2015 the IMF described recent growth as sluggish, and it linked the swings in growth since the mid-1990s to uneven harvests, outside shocks and supply bottlenecks.

citations.title: Making Senegal a Hub for West Africa

citations.title: Making Senegal a Hub for West Africa

threads.title: The Plan Sénégal Emergent
threads.text: In the mid-2010s the government launched a new development plan to make the country a hub for West Africa. By late 2015 the IMF saw growth breaking with its historical pace, helped by the plan's first steps, trade with Mali and cheaper oil, and income per person grew 2.7 percent a year over 2016–2025.

citations.title: Making Senegal a Hub for West Africa

threads.title: Oil and gas arrive
threads.text: Oil began flowing from the offshore Sangomar field in June 2024, and 2025 was the first full year of oil and gas output. Together with a better harvest, this lifted growth in 2025, when income per person rose 4.3 percent, the fastest rise since 2017. The World Bank expects growth to slow as oil output eases from its 2025 peak.

threads.title: Hidden debt and a suspended programme
threads.text: Government-led investigations found that public spending and debt in 2019–2023 had been much larger than reported, which raised borrowing costs and brought credit rating downgrades. The IMF suspended its lending programme in October 2024, and in 2026 the government was still seeking a new one.

since_last_year.text: Oil and gas output and a farm rebound lifted growth in 2025, and income per person rose 4.3 percent. In April 2026 the World Bank expected growth to slow in 2026 as oil output eased from its 2025 peak, and in June 2026 the IMF said that higher world oil prices after the start of the war in the Middle East would add pressure on public finances.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe strong output growth in the late 1990s, yet in the data income per person fell 0.4 percent in 1996 and rose only 0.6 percent in 1997, so a fast-growing population appears to have absorbed much of the gain. A similar gap shows in 2025: the sources report a larger jump in total output from oil and gas than the 4.3 percent rise in income per person.
